glosses: lachrymose, plaintive, tearful, weepy, prone to crying
Tearful, sorrowful, sad, pertaining to tears, weeping, causing tears or crying.

examples.text: It is true that Limeans were given to interpolating trivial songs into the most exquisite comedies and some lachrymose effects into the austerest music; but at least they never submitted to the boredom of a misplaced veneration.
a typically plaintive song from Radiohead
I can see by your plaintive smile something is wrong, so spill it.

glosses: Accompanied by tears; crying, or about to cry.

examples.text: Aaron got a little tearful until Laura came to reassure him.

The week that was yet to elapse, she spent in wandering through her uncle's favourite walks in hours of tearful vigil, beside his tomb, and in collecting together every trifle on which he had set a value.
Receiving the news of Joseph Beam's death two days after Christmas was a piercing blow that sent me into a tearful and contemplative stupor from which I have not yet emerged.

glosses: Inclined to weep; tearful or lachrymose.
Of a film or book etc.: full of tragic melodrama.

examples.text: When Tomorrow Comes was probably some sort of weepy love story which always got him laughing like a drain, often leading to his physical removal from the one and nines.

glosses: present participle and gerund of whimper
The sound of one who whimpers; a whimper; a feeble complaint.

examples.text: And my sea-birds made a great confusion in the awful calm, filling it with flashing pinions and plaintive whimperings, and settling into the shape of a dome all formed of beating wings, in which I on my ship and the tridentiferous god of the sea were enclosed, face to face.
